# Orphaned documents and range deletion — facts

> Source-anchored units about Orphaned documents and range deletion: 11 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · 11 units · 5 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB issue SERVER-130130 reports that recipient-side orphan bookkeeping can drift below the true count when a migration delete entry matches no recipient document. Jira lists the issue as unresolved for affected 6.0.0, 7.0.0, and 8.0.0 versions; it describes a bookkeeping defect, not direct user-data loss. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-130130 · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion
- [statement] Range deletion follows the ownership metadata handoff asynchronously. MongoDB waits for relevant open cursors before deleting the source copy, and the balancer can start a later range migration while an earlier delete phase is still pending. Open cursors can delay cleanup, and large range deletions can cause cache and I/O stress. Current MongoDB documentation says cleanup is resilient to a replica-set primary crash or restart. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/ · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion · also: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/dts/support/how-do-you-clean-up-orphaned-documents-in-a-mongodb-sharded-cluster

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The current MongoDB manual marks cleanupOrphaned deprecated starting in 8.0. The command runs on a shard primary, waits for orphan cleanup across the namespace, and does not directly start deletion; it must not run on mongos. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/cleanupOrphaned/ · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/cleanuporphaned-doesnt-seem-to-be-doing-what-i-want/8076
- [statement] Range cleanup can wait on open cursors: the current balancer procedure deletes the source copy only after open cursors on the range are gone. A MongoDB 3.4 forum response explains that an already-being-processed-for-deletion response typically means a query still holds a cursor; the response alone does not establish a failure. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/ · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/cleanuporphaned-doesnt-seem-to-be-doing-what-i-want/8076
- [statement] The MongoDB 9.0 manual marks cleanupOrphaned deprecated since 8.0 and says it waits for all orphaned documents in the namespace to be cleaned from a majority of the shard's replica-set members; it does not delete them directly. Alibaba's 2026 upgrade guide says MongoDB 4.4 introduced automatic migration recovery and that cleanupOrphaned can verify the background cleanup. Apply version-specific guidance before using older cleanup loops. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/cleanupOrphaned/ · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion · also: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/support/why-i-need-to-upgrade-my-instance-to-a-later-mongodb-version

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A range migration updates ownership metadata before the source shard deletes its old copy; the balancer deletes that copy after no open cursors remain. These leftover source copies are orphaned documents and consume disk while range deletion is pending. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/ · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-clean-up-orphaned-documents-sharded/view
- [statement] MongoDB 8.2 documentation sets orphanCleanupDelaySecs to 3600 seconds by default and terminateSecondaryReadsOnOrphanCleanup to true. The source shard waits for existing primary reads and then the delay before deleting orphans; secondaries terminate reads that began before migration commit. If that termination setting is disabled, a secondary read may silently miss moved documents; long-running reads may otherwise receive QueryPlanKilled and need to resume. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/long-running-secondary-reads/ · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters/
- [statement] One MongoDB 3.4 operator reported cleanupOrphaned running for three days across more than 100 shards, with rangeDeleter logs often showing zero deletions. This is a single 2018 report, not an expected duration for current versions. (low confidence) — https://dba.stackexchange.com/questions/209437/mongodb-cleanuporphaned-running-for-days · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion
- [statement] MongoDB issue SERVER-78703 documents a historical count behavior where numOrphans stayed at its pre-deletion value until range deletion finished, so the tracked count could exceed the remaining documents during cleanup. The issue lists fixes in 7.0.0-rc7 and 7.1.0-rc0. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-78703 · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion
- [statement] MongoDB defines orphaned documents as documents on a shard that also exist in chunks on other shards. They can remain on a former donor while range cleanup is incomplete after ownership moves. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-orphaned-document · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion · also: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/support/why-i-need-to-upgrade-my-instance-to-a-later-mongodb-version
- [statement] Starting in MongoDB 8.2, long-running secondary reads can be terminated before orphan deletion to avoid missing documents; the default orphanCleanupDelaySecs also increased from 900 seconds to 3600 seconds. Applications with long-running secondary reads should account for version-specific termination behavior during chunk migrations. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/long-running-secondary-reads/ · keywords: Orphaned documents and range deletion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/
